t: Maximum Points Tourist Can Earn — Day-by-Day DP
o: Over exactly k days, the tourist either stays (earning stayScore[i][curr]) or moves (earning travelScore[curr][dest]), starting anywhere. Example 2: start at city 1, stay day 0 (+4), travel to city 2 day 1 (+4) = 8. State (day, city) with transitions from every previous city gives an O(k n^2) DP — at most 200*200*200 = 8M operations, well within limits.
k: dp[i][c] = best total after day i ending at city c; each day independently takes max(stay, best move over all predecessors).

a.i: Initialize day 0 as max(stay there, arrive from anywhere). For subsequent days, dp[i][c] = max(dp[i-1][c] + stayScore[i][c], max over p of dp[i-1][p] + travelScore[p][c]). The answer is the max over cities on the last day.
s: For each later day i and city c, take the max of staying and the best incoming travel edge.
Return max of the final dp array.
a.t: O(k*n^2) — for each of k days and n cities we relax n predecessor edges.
a.sp: O(n) — two rolling arrays of city states.

w: This is a textbook layered-graph longest-path DP; the free choice of start is absorbed by initializing day 0 as the best of stay-or-arrive. Pitfalls: forgetting that staying is also allowed on day 0, and confusing travelScore indices (travelScore[from][to]). Follow-up: reconstruct the itinerary, or add constraints like visiting each city at most once (which would require bitmask DP).
